data.title: Dumping to stacking in just three months? What’s going on with XRP whales?
data.description:
XRP’s price dipped under $1, and most of the market looks ready to walk away. Not the whales, though. At least not yet.

Is that enough to stop the fall?

Whales are pulling their stash off Binance!

According to recent data, XRP whales have taken out more than $127 million in XRP off Binance since 10th November. Net outflows went between $12-$33 million over the past week, including about $21 million on the 16th alone!

Not too long ago, it was the other way around.

In August, XRP went up by about 72% and back above $1.50. Whales were dumping as much as $75 million on Binance in a single day!

If you look further back, you’ll see that XRP hit $3.55 in the summer of 2025. In that time, some days saw more than $100 million flood in.

One day even hit close to $270 million.

When coins leave an exchange, people usually want to hold. However, don’t get excited yet. Some of this might just be Binance moving its money around.

Remember when it was topping up its reserves after the October hack?

Lowest weekly close in two years…

data.title: Solana Foundation takes ‘majority interest’ in CoinGecko – What changes next?
data.description:
The Solana Foundation now holds a “majority interest” in CoinGecko, its Chief Product Officer Vibhu Norby said on X.

CoinGecko described the arrangement as “backing” when it announced the news at Breakpoint in London on the 17th of November. Neither announcement gave the exact stake, price, or governance terms.

Four days earlier, CoinGecko had promoted independent ownership as a reason to choose its data service over Binance-owned CoinMarketCap. It now plans to explore trading alongside its market data.

Could users trade directly on CoinGecko?

The Foundation said it planned to bring Solana-powered trading to CoinGecko’s website, app, and GeckoTerminal. Notably, CoinGecko said it was still exploring trading features.

For Solana, that could mean reaching traders where they already look up prices. CoinGecko draws well over 50 million monthly sessions, according to the Foundation.

On the 17th of November, Solana [SOL] recorded $50.44 billion in 30-day DEX spot volume, whereas Ethereum [ETH] recorded $53.86 billion.

Norby also flagged broader coverage of stocks and real-world assets [RWAs]. AMBCrypto reported that Solana’s RWA value reached $5 billion in October.

By the 12th of November, tokenized equity supply stood at $607 million, with xStocks accounting for 75%.

Who sets CoinGecko’s data rules?

CoinGecko’s API guide warned that exchange ownership could raise questions about bias in rankings and trading volumes. AMBCrypto covered similar concerns when Binance bought CoinMarketCap in 2020.

After Norby’s disclosure, an X user called the new arrangement “a credibility problem.”

CoinGecko said its methods would stay “transparent, publicly accessible.” Readers can check how it calculates prices, but the announcements leave open who can approve changes to those rules.

Brera Holdings disclosed board rights in a separate 2025 deal involving Solmate. A later filing specified that the Foundation could nominate up to two directors, depending on board size. For CoinGecko, board seats and approval rights remain undisclosed.

Final Summary

  • The Solana Foundation, according to its product chief, Vibhu Norby. Four days earlier, CoinGecko had promoted its independent ownership.
  • They plan to add Solana-powered trading to CoinGecko. CoinGecko says the rules it uses to calculate prices will stay public.

data.title: Bitcoin tests $62K support – Can BTC bulls hold without Spot demand?
data.description:
After the $3 billion crypto liquidation wave that occurred on the 13th and 14th of November, the liquidation numbers have slowed slightly.

A relatively small liquidation number of just over $563 million was recorded on the 15th, and just $289.9 million in liquidations across the market on the 16th of November, according to CoinGlass data.

AMBCrypto reported recently that the Bitcoin [BTC] price move down to $62k acted as a leverage flush. It remains to be seen whether the bulls can enforce a recovery from here.

THIS supply cluster could keep BTC’s revival hopes alive

In a post on X, Glassnode showed that the price was trading just above a dense cluster of short-term holder supply. The darker cells denote more BTC supply in STH custody at that cost basis.

The $62k-$63k area was a particularly dense STH supply cluster, and in recent days, there has been a positive reaction. The same area had been the base of the previous impulse move higher in mid-August.

If this area is breached, it could lead to another capitulation and new lows being formed.

Sustained demand is necessary to stabilize Bitcoin price trends

Crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. noted that the bulls were trying to push BTC prices higher in the futures market. The hourly taker buy-sell imbalance reached +8,709 BTC on Monday, the 16th of November.

Yet, the price was yet to push higher. The first areas of interest were the imbalance at $66.2k-$66.9k and the local high at $70,214.

Deeply negative apparent demand (30-day sum), with a 30-day reading of -247,700 BTC and a yearly measurement of -1.21 million BTC, highlighted severe market stress.

Crypto analyst Darkfost wrote that the metric, which is an indirect on-chain proxy based on new issuance versus changes in supply inactive for over a year, does not measure net cash outflows.

Nevertheless, it has historically been a reliable indicator that helps confirm trend strength. Right now, any price rebound without apparent demand easing toward neutral or positive levels would signal weakness.

Final Summary

  • The Bitcoin price sank to $62k, a dense pocket of short-term holder supply, and has managed to bounce to $65k in the past 48 hours.
  • There is short-term futures demand, but sustained demand is lacking and continues to signal buyer weakness.

data.title: Here’s how Ledger’s website was hit by the Optimizely malware attack
data.description:
On the 16th of November, Ledger’s public website was infected with malware designed to swap crypto addresses and steal card details. Security researcher Scott Helme traced the code to Optimizely, a website testing provider. His team found compromised scripts tied to 178 organizations, including Ledger, the BBC, and Zoom.

How was Ledger’s website affected?

In practice, the malware could swap a copied crypto address for one belonging to the attacker. So if a visitor pasted that address and approved the payment, their crypto could go to the attacker instead.

So far, researchers have traced the malware to Ledger’s public website. Whether it also affected Ledger’s hardware wallets or the Ledger Wallet app remains unclear.

Just over a month earlier, though, Ledger had faced a separate attack involving physical devices. In that case, Ledger confirmed that some wallets sold through a reseller contained unauthorized hardware.

At the time, AMBCrypto reported that the October theft had reached $91 million across more than 470 crypto addresses.

Report URI recorded the cleanup of Ledger’s script at 20:41 UTC that day. Early on the 17th of November, Optimizely said,

We’ve fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects.

How much crypto did victims lose?

Report URI traced about $7,040 in crypto to addresses linked to the attack on the 16th of November. When Galaxy Digital’s Alex Thorn looked at where the money came from, he estimated that victims sent about $2,300. He said,

Most of the rest was the attacker’s own money. The attacker appears to have been very sloppy with their onchain hygiene

However, the number of Ledger visitors who lost funds remains unclear.

What happened at Polymarket?

A similar breach had hit Polymarket a few weeks earlier. In that case, the malicious code could act on behalf of traders who were already signed in.

On the 29th of October, it sold some traders’ positions and moved funds out of their wallets.

Polymarket paused international trading to stop further losses. It later announced $3.9 million in reimbursements, including about $1.2 million for losses during the pause. By the 30th of October, the company said it had fully refunded 689 of the 726 affected wallets.

Final Summary

  • Ledger’s website served malware in an attack that reached 178 organizations.
  • However, losses among Ledger visitors remain unknown.

data.title: Top 13 Telegram games to try out in November 2026
data.description:
Telegram has become more than just a communication app for people around the world. What started out as just a messaging app has grown into an ecosystem of its own. Users can enjoy casual games, puzzles, and simulation-based games. Accessibility is another key reason why players are attracted to Telegram games; it has an easy point of entry and reward mechanisms as well.

Here are our top picks for the best Telegram games in the month of November 2026:

1. Chat Wars

Chat Wars is a traditional role-playing game that is built around fantasy world-building, heroes, guilds, resources, and strategic decisions. Players start by building their characters and can collect resources, improve equipment, participate in activities, and contribute to their guild.

Combat, crafting, and resource management are all part of the game’s overall experience, so players can become part of a larger experience rather than just collecting points. Guild participation is a major part of the game, and groups can cooperate, coordinate, and work towards shared objectives.

2. Catizen

Catizen lets users develop, combine, and manage digital cats. The main objective of the game is to collect new cats, merge similar ones, expand facilities, complete missions, and grow. Players can collect rewards, unlock new buildings, and participate in seasonal events.

The game has a more holistic approach than many other tap-to-earn games as it focuses on community interactions and long-term engagement. The game has evolved over time into an ecosystem of its own with a native token called CATI.

3. Hamster Kombat

A very popular game in the space, Hamster Kombat also has a tap-to-earn format where the original gameplay revolved around managing a virtual crypto exchange owned by a CEO who was a hamster. Now the experience has evolved into HamsterVerse, bringing additional games and experiences into the ecosystem.

One such experience is Hamster GameDev, which allows players to manage a virtual game development studio where they can hire team members, create games, upgrade their operations, and generate virtual income. Instead of a repeated tapping gaming, this gives it a more structured managment style traditional approach.

4. Pig of Ton

Pig of Ton is a hyper-casual merge-and-battle game that integrates character collection, merging mechanics, and competitive rankings. The game has futuristic cyber pigs that can be collected, upgraded, and developed, and are a central part of the gameplay.

The futuristic pig theme gives it a very distinct identity in the space, and instead of using traditional fantasy characters, cyber pigs are its central characters.

5. PlayDeck

PlayDeck has a large collection of casual games in a single Telegram Mini App, making it convenient for players who enjoy playing in new genres. It gives players a chance to explore challenges, puzzles, and reaction-based games.

PlayDeck offers convenience and accessibility to all its users and can compete with other open PlayBoxes, spin the Wheel of Luck, and earn $PlayCoin.

6. MemeFi

MemeFi is a tap-to-earn combat game where players fight meme-inspired bosses, earn crypto rewards, and make character progressions. The main USP of the game is its combat, where players go up against enemies and defeat challenging opponents.

Users can also create various clans, manage their energy levels, or use boosters. MEMEFI is the utility and governance token of the platform and has a total supply of 10 billion.

7. Rocky Rabbit 

Rocky Rabbit is a tap-to-earn mini-game that was built on the TON network. Players need to train their rabbits in the game, participate in duels and complete any tasks to rank higher. The game takes its inspiration from fitness and boxing.

The platform’s native token RBTC (RabBitcoin) was launched on TON in 2024, and players can join competitions and battles, earn rewards, and bonuses for referrals.

8. Yescoin

A famous retro-style pixel mini-game on TON, Yescoin lets users swipe their fingers across the screen to catch falling coins similar to Fruit Ninja. Players can complete missions, collect coins, upgrade their skills, and be a part of the community.

Players can buy upgrades and power-ups to boost their earnings, as it is managed by an energy system that regenerates over time. There are quests, missions, events, and various other options for players to earn rewards throughout the game.

9. TONs of Dungeons 

A play-to-earn mini-game built around the Minesweeper mechanics that mixes it with dungeon exploration. Players need to explore a 5×5 grid where they tap blocks one by one and earn gold. If they choose the block that has a trap, the game is over.

As a bonus after every round, there is an option to play a clicker side game where players need to tap the skull to farm gold. Besides the game itself, players can collect keys for passive income and tickets for daily cash prizes.

10. Pixel Tap 

Pixel Tap is a cyberpunk combat-themed mini-game where players can tap the screen to earn in-game coins, upgrade robot fighters, and take part in real-time battles against each other. It is part of the wider Pixelverse ecosystem, and the game revolves around tapping mechanics and PvP battles.

In-game currency can be earned through referrals, daily tasks, battles, and general activity. Players can get into battles and earn points and tokens in PvE and PvP settings. $PIXFI is the native token of the platform, and rewards can be earned in it.

11. Egg Drop 

Egg Drop is a play-to-earn game on the BNB Chain where players drop virtual eggs into target zones and score points while collecting points and levelling up “Birdies”. The eggs fall under various categories, such as white, yellow, royal, energy, punch, shield, attack, and steal types.

Accessibility and engagement are important parts of the game where the sessions are short and easy to navigate and aimed at users looking for time-intensive games. Token incentives and collected items can be accumulated through regular activity in the game.

12. RollerTap

RollerTap has a tapping mechanism where players collect RCC or Roller Community Coins that are in-app currency. The rewards can be used to increase their tap level and how much they earn overtime creating a system built around steady activity and upgrades.

Leaderboards in the game also allow players to compete with each other and track their rankings. They can also collect cards that boost their profits and take part in limited eveents and challenges for extra rewards.

13. Bombie

A post-apocalyptical setup where players have to survive the zombie attack and earn the $Bombie token, this Telegram game was launched in 2024. The objective is simple: shoot the zombies, defeat the bosses, and upgrade your weapons and gears.

Players can earn the token through the play-to-earn model and also by taking part in airdrops and boss raids. There are community events that help players interact with each other as well.

Conclusion

Telegram games give an easy and convenient way for players to engage with a lot of these tap-to-earn apps. They started out as simple games and have evolved into much more complex ecosystems of their own overtime, offering a wide variety of gaming experience.

Each game brings something different and can be appealing to a different type of gamer. However, it is advisable to do your own reseach before monetarily investing in any game.

data.title: XRP loses August swing low, but here’s why its price could bottom near $0.78
data.description:
XRP has been deeply affected by the crypto market’s sell-offs in recent weeks. Towards the end of September, when Bitcoin [BTC] was challenging the $87K resistance level, XRP bulls were trying to establish a foothold above the $1.50 supply zone.

They pushed the price as high as $1.65, but could not go any higher. The subsequent selling, fueled by fear and cascading liquidation waves, has driven XRP back below a swing low that is both technically and psychologically important.

XRP faces bearish price structure shift, while an analyst called a market bottom

XRP’s bullish price structure shift in August (green) originated at the swing low at $0.99 (orange). The same low was breached during the selling in recent weeks.

The CMF slipped below -0.05 to signal heavy capital outflows earlier in November. The Awesome Oscillator was also well below the zero line, highlighting intense southbound momentum.

Against this bearish backdrop on the daily timeframe, crypto analyst and trader Ali Martinez posted an encouraging chart. The weekly timeframe has formed an ascending triangle pattern over the past five years.

The rising trendline of the triangle is about to be tested, and could be the long-term bottom. His prediction suggested that the current dip could extend to $0.78.

Here, it’s worth noting that the analyst’s call for a market bottom was accompanied by net buying on Coinbase. As well as a TD Sequential buy signal on the daily timeframe.

XRP price prediction — Look to sell the bounce!

The 4-hour chart was also bearish alongside the daily timeframe. The drop to $0.893 saw a bounce to $0.95 in just few days. The CMF also moved into neutral territory, while the Awesome Oscillator’s green histogram bars suggested that bearish momentum was weak.

A price move above $1.0 would be an indication of a corrective bounce. Such a bounce is likely to reach $1.13 and $1.28, the notable imbalances overhead. This would also happen to align somewhat well with the Fibonacci retracement levels.

Final Summary

  • XRP might be approaching a long-term rising trendline support around $0.78, which could mark a market bottom.
  • Short-term bias for the altcoin has been bearish, and traders can look to sell a bounce towards $1.13-$1.28.

data.title: Zcash price eyes $940 – Can ZEC turn its relief rally into a recovery?
data.description:
Zcash [ZEC] has been moving against the grain of the broader crypto market, gaining 2.86% over the past 24 hours while Bitcoin [BTC] slipped 0.07% and the overall market continued to trade flat. This suggested the recovery was specific to ZEC rather than a result of improving market-wide sentiment.

However, the rebound came after a steep correction, as ZEC is down 19.85% over the past seven days. With no fresh catalyst to explain the move, the gains seem to be a short-term relief rally. The question now is whether buyers can sustain this recovery.

Can Zcash hold its daily recovery?

On the daily chart, bulls have started fighting back as short-term momentum picks up. At the time of writing, ZEC traded at $921.75, remaining within the lowest Fibonacci retracement band. This indicated that the recovery was still weak and left the broader bearish structure intact.

OBV showed a modest uptick after its sharp decline, while the RSI climbed to 35.41, suggesting selling pressure had eased but not enough for buyers to gain the upper hand in the market.

Zcash approaches a key H4 resistance level

The H4 chart offered a closer look at the token’s recent recovery, with ZEC trending towards the 23.6% Fibonacci level at $939.93. If the bulls can successfully break above this resistance, it would strengthen the bullish case and bring the daily $1,013 level into focus.

The MACD turned positive, while OBV began to stabilize after its steep decline. However, the lack of a stronger OBV recovery suggests buying volume has yet to fully support the improving momentum.

Final Summary

  • Zcash’s short-term recovery is gaining traction, but the daily chart shows that the broader bearish structure remains intact.
  • Holding above $906 and breaking the $939-$940 resistance could open the way towards $945-$971.

data.title: ‘Whole new set of risks’ – How Lighter recovered $5M USDC after API leak
data.description:
On the 16th of November, Lighter reopened withdrawals after an attacker gained control of a trader’s API keys.

In its report, the perpetual futures exchange said its Security Council returned about 5 million USDC to the affected trader. Interestingly, deposits and withdrawals were “back to normal” after the council switched off Guardian mode.

The exchange traced the leak to unofficial signing software and said its protocol and smart contracts were, fortunately enough, unaffected.

What did Lighter’s withdrawal pause recover?

Lighter said it had paused withdrawals through Guardian mode. That basically allowed its Security Council to return around 5 million USDC.

The exchange said it was also working to recover funds linked to “an additional withdrawal attempt by the attacker.” However, a separate withdrawal of 10.39 million USDC had already gone through on Ethereum [ETH] before the pause was announced. Bubblemaps later traced some of those funds to Hyperliquid [HYPE].

Kevin Wang, a former market maker at Lighter, also weighed in on the incident. He wrote,

Lighter said it now required a wallet signature to move funds into public pools.

How did Lighter’s token react?

At the time of writing, Lighter [LIT] traded near $3, about 8% above its pre-incident range of $2.77–$2.78. LIT had rebounded about 29% from a brief wick near $2.33.

 

The rebound had already stalled near $3.07 on the hourly chart. An hourly close above that level would extend the recovery.

Did traders pull back after withdrawals reopened?

With LIT recovering, the dollar value of assets held on Lighter did not react the same way. On the 17th of November 2026, DeFiLlama showed Total Value Locked (TVL) of $671.04 million. That was down about 14% from $777.33 million before the incident.

Of course, derivatives activity also cooled around the incident. On the 16th of November, Open Interest fell 9% to $559.99 million, leaving less value in outstanding positions. Daily Perp Volume dropped 15% to $3.147 billion, showing fewer dollars traded in perpetual futures.

Final Summary

  • Lighter’s withdrawals resumed after its Security Council returned about 5 million USDC.
  • LIT rebounded while Open Interest and trading volume fell.

data.title: Why Chainlink price faces a make-or-break test at the $8.88 level
data.description:
In the recent selloff, Chainlink [LINK] token prices fell to a low of $8.57 on Saturday, the 14th of November. The downtrend from October to the first week of November accelerated over the past ten days.

Driven by fear prevailing across the crypto markets, led by heavy Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] losses, LINK fell below the long-term swing support of $10.61.

Intensified selling accompanied by LINK exchange withdrawals

Crypto analyst FundingVest observed that certain altcoins saw sizeable outflows from Binance. Chainlink was one of them. By comparison, Bitcoin saw moderate inflows while Ethereum showed slight outflows.

Shrinking supply on exchanges was a bullish signal for the altcoin, even though it ceded the $10.61 swing level to the bears. However, it is not a guarantee of a price rally by itself.

The exchange outflows are overshadowed by the persistent heating signal on the spot volume bubble map. Red bubbles signal increased trading activity in LINK markets.

Heating volume signals alongside a steady price correction from $14.3 to $10.6, a 25.7% decline in just over a month, was a sign of sustained selling.

Such pressure on LINK might be difficult to shrug off, especially now that the price structure was also bearish.

Will the Chainlink price prediction come true?

Earlier this month, AMBCrypto had drawn attention to the $10.61-$10.87 area. Key swing levels here marked it as a demand zone, one that bulls managed to defend in late October.

The weekly structure was bullish, though the altcoin has witnessed a deep correction. Using the impulse move higher to $15.77 earlier this year, Fibonacci retracement levels were plotted.

Additionally, this rally in August had also left behind an imbalance (white) that was being tested at the time of writing.

A bullish reaction from $8.88, the 78.6% retracement level inside the fair value gap, would be a strong sign of a bullish reversal. However, a weekly session close below $8.40 would be a warning sign that bearish pressure remained dominant.

Final Summary

  • Chainlink faced heightened spot trading volume during its 25% price decline that began in late September, showing heightened selling pressure.
  • The price correction has reached a pivotal demand zone on the weekly chart, and a bullish reaction from here appears likely.

data.title: Tokenized stocks are exactly where stablecoins were in 2020 – How?
data.description:
Stablecoins started as a way to hold dollars on-chain. Then people started lending, trading, and earning with them. In time, DeFi grew up around them.

Tokenized stocks are heading down the same route now, and the resemblance is uncanny.

Tokenized stocks in DeFi grew 24x to $300M in a year!

What’s worth noting here is how much of it is actually being used.

According to data from Token Terminal, tokenized stocks deposited into DeFi are now worth about $300 million. A year ago, that was at approx. $12.5 million.

This number didn’t move at all through late 2025. Things picked up in the spring, blasted through $100 million by around August, and then shot past a quarter million in September.

It’s also a bigger share of the market now. That $300 million is 6.3% of the $4.8 billion tokenized stock market cap. Last year, only 2.4% was being put to work.

So, why move stocks into DeFi at all?

Because once they’re there, holders can borrow against them, earn fees by providing liquidity, or chase yield.

And every new way to use them, is essentially one more reason not to cash out.

Tokenized stocks are at the same spot stablecoins were back in 2020

A fun comparison here.

Tokenized stocks now have a market cap of about $4.8 billion. Stablecoins crossed that exact number in March 2020. Since then, stablecoins have grown, 59 times over! The number is at $285 billion now.

Tokenized stocks are moving fast too. They were worth only a few tens of millions in early 2025.

But why? A blockchain is basically a ledger for assets, and it gets more useful when it holds things people really want. U.S Stocks are about as in-demand as it gets.

Stablecoins survived four crashes, will tokenized stock do the same?

Stablecoins didn’t get to where they are without the effort.

They made it through the COVID crash, the Terra collapse, FTX, and the USDC de-peg after SVB failed. Market cap fell by 28% between February 2022 and October 2023, then spiked up to a high by September 2024.

What kept them going though? Cash and T-bill reserves backed every token, plus people who actually wanted to use them.

Tokenized stocks follow the same 1:1 idea.

Except the risk factor is higher. So is the potential for gains.

Final Summary

  • Tokenized stocks in DeFi grew 24x to $300 million in a year.
  • This is where stablecoins were in March 2020.
